generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The introduction of the member variable `unionFieldAttributes` makes the `ResolveUnionTypes` rule stateful. If this rule instance is shared across threads or reused for different plan analyses, it will cause race conditions and data corruption. This state should be managed within the scope of the `apply` method (e.g., by passing it as a parameter to `doRule`) rather than as a class member.

Changing the return value from a list containing an `UnresolvedAttribute` to throwing an `IllegalStateException` shifts the error handling strategy from "error collection" to "fail-fast". This prevents the analyzer from collecting and reporting multiple issues in a single pass, potentially degrading the user experience by only revealing one ambiguity at a time.

review_comment: Not sure I understand why p should be resolved, while p.children should be unresolved. Should it not be `p -> p.resolved() == false || p.childrenResolved() == false ? p : doRule(p)`

This was carried over from `AnalyzerRule` and `BaseAnalyzerRule` while collapsing their execution logic into this simple `Rule`.

Currently it says "I'll just return the current plan without changes (i.e. skip) if it's either already resolved or has yet-to-be resolved children". I think this is correct.
